Operation 'sendBroadcast' has semantic quality issues: vague_summary, missing_output_details. Original summary 'Send or schedule' is too vague and doesn't convey the action clearly. Description is comprehensive but dense and difficult for AI agents to parse. Improved summary uses action verbs and clarifies the dual behavior. Improved description reorganizes information into logical sections (immediate send vs. scheduled, token validation, preflight checks) with clearer explanation of return codes and error conditions for better AI agent interpretability.

data.current_description:
Sends now (**202**, `status` shows how far it got) or, with `send_at`, schedules it (**200**,
`status: scheduled`). Emails real people and cannot be undone.

With a `confirmation_token` from `prepare`, nothing goes out unless the broadcast, its status,
the `send_at` (or its absence) and its recipient count (within the token's `tolerance`) still
match what was prepared, and the same key prepared it: otherwise a 422 on
`confirmation_token` says what changed. The token is optional here so an integration with
its own review step can send directly; MCP always requires it.

Preflight runs again either way: a 422 on `campaign` lists what would stop the send. That
includes a send larger than what is left of this month's email allowance: extra emails are a
charge the founder approves in the dashboard before sending, so the API never buys them.
data.summary_suggestion: Send broadcast immediately or schedule for later
data.description_suggestion: Sends a broadcast immediately (returns 202 with in-progress status) or schedules it for a future time with `send_at` (returns 200 with scheduled status). Emails are sent to real contacts and cannot be undone. Optionally accepts a `confirmation_token` from the prepare operation to validate that the broadcast, recipient count, and send time match what was previously prepared; if validation fails, returns 422 with details of what changed. Runs preflight validation to check campaign readiness and email allowance; returns 422 if send would exceed monthly allowance or other campaign issues exist.
data.reasoning: Original summary 'Send or schedule' is too vague and doesn't convey the action clearly. Description is comprehensive but dense and difficult for AI agents to parse. Improved summary uses action verbs and clarifies the dual behavior. Improved description reorganizes information into logical sections (immediate send vs. scheduled, token validation, preflight checks) with clearer explanation of return codes and error conditions for better AI agent interpretability.

data.current_description:
Stops a sending broadcast where it is. Already-sent emails stand; a batched broadcast keeps
its schedule for `resume`. A broadcast that is not sending is a 409 and nothing changes.
data.summary_suggestion: Pause an in-progress broadcast
data.description_suggestion: Pauses a broadcast that is currently sending, halting further email delivery at the current point. Already-sent emails remain delivered. For batched broadcasts, the schedule is preserved for later resumption. Returns 200 on success. Returns 409 if the broadcast is not in a sending state (e.g., already paused, scheduled, or completed), with no state changes.

else is a 409 and nothing changes.

data.current_description:
Identity is deliberately not editable. It is resolved, not assigned, so changing it would
mean changing who a row is about.

Moving `stage` to your invited stage mints a real invitation code as a side effect, exactly
as the dashboard does, so the invite email that fires next has a working link.

A contact hidden past the plan's contact size is refused with a **403**, `code:
contact_hidden`, `param: contact`, and nothing is written. It is saved, and editing works
again once the workspace moves up a size. Deleting it still works.
data.summary_suggestion: Update contact attributes and stage
data.description_suggestion: Modifies a contact's attributes such as email, name, custom fields, and stage. Identity cannot be changed as it determines which contact record is being updated. Moving a contact to an invited stage automatically mints an invitation code and triggers the invite email workflow. Returns the updated contact object. Contacts hidden due to plan size limits return a 403 error and are not modified. Note: This operation fires the same submission pipeline as dashboard edits, including canonicalization, deduplication, and automation triggers.
data.reasoning: Original summary is too generic. Description is detailed but scattered across multiple concerns without clear structure. Improved version clarifies what can be updated, explains the identity constraint, documents the stage-to-invitation side effect, and explains error handling. Better organized for AI agent decision-making about when to use this operation.

message: Operation 'deleteContact' has semantic quality issues: vague_summary, missing_input_details, missing_output_details. Summary conflates two distinct operations (removal vs. erasure). Description lacks clarity about the parameter and return value. Improved version distinguishes the two modes clearly, explains the business impact of each (billable count, referral graph), and clarifies the irreversibility of erasure for AI agent decision-making.

data.current_description:
By default this is a recoverable removal that frees the billable count and keeps the shape
of the referral graph, so nobody's position moves.

With `?erase=true` it is the GDPR Article 17 erasure instead: identity is overwritten in
place across the contact, its submissions and its campaign sends, and it cannot be undone.
data.summary_suggestion: Delete or erase a contact record
data.description_suggestion: Removes a contact from the audience. By default, deletion is recoverable: the contact is removed from billable count and the referral graph structure is preserved, so other contacts' leaderboard positions remain unchanged. With `?erase=true`, performs GDPR Article 17 erasure instead: identity data is irreversibly overwritten across the contact record, all submissions, and all campaign sends. Erasure cannot be undone. Returns 200 on success.
data.reasoning: Summary conflates two distinct operations (removal vs. erasure). Description lacks clarity about the parameter and return value. Improved version distinguishes the two modes clearly, explains the business impact of each (billable count, referral graph), and clarifies the irreversibility of erasure for AI agent decision-making.

data.current_description:
Every email this person was sent or is queued to get, newest first: broadcasts, automation
steps and system emails such as the confirmation or an invitation. Each row says where it
came from, its subject, its delivery status and when it was sent and delivered.

Opens and clicks are not included. Tracking is off by default, so an empty value would
read as "never opened" when the truth is "never measured". Page with the `msg_…` id of a
row as `starting_after` or `ending_before`.
data.description_suggestion: Returns all emails sent to or queued for a contact, ordered newest first. Includes broadcasts, automation steps, and system emails (confirmations, invitations). Each record contains source, subject, delivery status, send time, and delivery time. Note: Opens and clicks are not included in responses. Tracking is disabled by default, so empty tracking fields indicate "not measured" rather than "never occurred". Pagination uses the `msg_…` message id as cursor anchors via `starting_after` or `ending_before` parameters.
data.reasoning: Summary is adequate. Description is comprehensive but could be better organized for AI agent clarity. Improved version separates what is returned from what is not, clarifies the tracking limitation upfront, and explicitly documents pagination mechanics. Helps agents understand data availability and cursor usage.

Rank, how many referrals it would take to reach first, and how many places one more

All values are read live from the leaderboard and represent a snapshot at query time—do not cache or store these values as they change with each referral event. Returns the position object with rank and projection fields.

Each record shows the automation reference, current step, and state information.
